haiku-low.q1: No difference: both return 401 with "Invalid email or password", and both run a bcrypt compare and record a failure.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 "Too many attempts" with no password check and no recorded attempt, until locked_until passes (15 minutes).
haiku-low.q3: If the request carried an old sid, its session row is deleted. A new session ID is generated and inserted, and the browser gets it.
haiku-low.q4: Only the session ID, no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: After 12 hours since login, even with continuous use. Activity only refreshes the 30-minute idle clock, not the 12-hour limit.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the row if one exists, returns 302 to /login, and clears the sid cookie with Max-Age=0.
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row by sid before responding. If already gone, that is a no-op; still 302 to /login and cookie cleared.
haiku-low.q8: In the shared Postgres sessions table, not process memory. Any instance finds the row by the sid cookie value.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that now minus last_seen_at is at most 30 minutes and now minus created_at is at most 12 hours. On valid, it sets last_seen_at to now.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 error page with no Set-Cookie header, so the user stays logged out.
haiku-low.q12: The hourly cleanup job deletes sessions idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours. Expired rows found during requests are also deleted.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ: both get 401 login page with "Invalid email or password". The server runs bcrypt against a dummy hash and records the failure, so timing and lockout behave the same.
sonnet.q2: It gets 429 Too many attempts (while locked, until locked_until, 15 min after the lock was set); the password is not checked and the attempt is not recorded.
sonnet.q3: If the password is correct, the old session row is deleted from sessions, and a new session with a new random ID is created.
sonnet.q4: Only the session ID (no user data). It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: After 12 hours since login (created_at); the idle limit of 30 min never triggers because of continuous use. They are redirected to /login.
sonnet.q6: Deletes the row if it exists, responds 302 to /login, and clears the sid cookie (Max-Age=0).
sonnet.q7: It deletes the session row by sid (no-op if already gone), then responds 302 to /login and clears the sid cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the shared Postgres database's sessions table (not process memory). Either instance reads the row by the session ID in the sid cookie.
sonnet.q9: In the login_failures table (one row per failed attempt: email, failed_at). The server counts that email's rows with failed_at within the 10 minutes ending now (sliding window, no stored window start).
sonnet.q10: It compares now with last_seen_at (at most 30 min) and with created_at (at most 12 h), and requires the row to exist. When valid it sets last_seen_at = now.
sonnet.q11: A 503 error page with no Set-Cookie, so the user stays logged out.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup job (run by any instance) deletes sessions idle over 30 min or older than 12 h. Expired sessions are also deleted if found on a request.
